editorial:
Imagine packing your bags and leaving your small town behind to start fresh in the big city. That is exactly what Shirlee Kenyon does when she heads to Chicago after dumping her boyfriend. In a wild turn of events, she ends up hosting a radio advice show and becomes an overnight hit because she tells it like it is. The catch is that the station makes her pretend to be a licensed doctor. You will love the tension as a curious reporter starts snooping around to find out if she is actually a fraud, only to realize he is falling hard for her. It is a lighthearted ride that feels like a warm hug from the early nineties.

The chemistry between the leads is the best part of the whole experience, making the romance feel real and sweet. While the plot is a bit predictable, the fast pacing keeps you from getting bored. If you enjoy stories about fake identities and accidental fame, you should definitely give this one a shot. It is a great pick for a cozy movie night.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the reporter finally discovers that Shirlee is not actually a doctor. Instead of exposing her to ruin her career, he realizes he truly loves her for her honesty and heart. Shirlee eventually comes clean to her listeners, and surprisingly, they still love her because her advice actually worked. She and the reporter end up together, proving that being yourself is better than any fake title.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cheesy 90s romances and underdog stories.
